before: Tracked deletion across paragraphs refused in collaboration, and tracked paragraph deletion refused everywhere. Stamping a paragraph mark replaced an existing w:pPr and w:rPr with new nodes.
after: Tracked deletion across paragraphs and tracked paragraph deletion work in collaboration. Stamping a paragraph mark keeps the existing w:pPr and w:rPr nodes, and the containers it creates use the mark id family so resolving the mark removes only those. Only the replica that stamped the mark recognizes those containers; a reject on another replica leaves them as empty elements, which every replica materializes the same way. Position markers between paragraphs no longer split one paragraph-mark deletion into several revision ids or review decisions. Accepting a deletion that joins two paragraphs moves body-level position markers between them into the joined paragraph as new nodes, so replicas apply a removal and an insertion. When several participants accept the same join at once, each writes its own copy of a relocated marker; each copy records the marker it replaced in the existing split lineage fields, and a paragraph shows only the first copy of one lineage in its text, or none while the original is listed again after an undo.
reason: No stored field, update, or format rule changes. The new edits are ordinary text, run, and property writes that released readers already apply, and keeping existing property nodes uses ordinary child splices. Concurrent creation of property elements relies on the paragraph text collaboration model this change builds on. Peers on different versions can show a different number of review cards for the same state, because grouping across position markers is a display rule; the shared state is the same. Where a marker lands on accept depends on the accepting peer's version; every replica still holds the same tree after the accept replicates. The duplicate-copy rule decides which conflicting node survives, which is repair semantics: a replica without it shows every copy. It uses the existing splitFrom and splitLineage fields and belongs to the unreleased repair version that the paragraph text format introduces, so it must ship in the same release as that format. Replicas on the released format cannot join those rooms, so no mixed room meets both rules; a later release that changed it again would need its own repair version.
